messages:
anya: Heads-up — customer asks keep coming for smaller payloads on mobile. asking if we can tighten the response envelope and make trace fields optional by default.
mike: +1. We should treat this as both an API contract and runtime perf problem. smaller envelope -> less tokens -> cheaper for customers.
raul: What do they mean by optional trace fields? we currently add full trace metadata: trace_id, parent_id, span, routing_hints, token_usage.
sara-pm: Customer use-case: telemetry is heavy on mobile. They only need trace_id for support, not full routing hints. They suggested sampling detailed traces at 1% and always keep a minimal trace_id.
anya: proposal: default response keeps minimal metadata: {"trace_id", "model", "token_usage.summary"}. full trace blob behind a query param or header (X-include-trace: full) or via server-side sampling.
mike: I like header toggle. Also want to rename token_usage to token_cost or token_summary? current field names are verbose. short names reduce payload too.
raul: be careful: renaming breaks customers. We should alias old fields for a deprecation window. e.g., keep token_usage but start returning token_summary too, then deprecate token_usage after N months.
sara-pm: Launch criteria idea: 1) default minimal envelope in beta across hosted API, 2) compatibility aliasing for 6 months, 3) opt-in header for full_metadata, 4) canary with two enterprise customers and one PLG power user.
anya: For structured output + tool calls: structured output objects must stay nested but we can gzip on the wire if content-type supports it. Noting mobile clients may not accept extra encodings.
mike: Another lever: slice out per-token counts only when sequence_length > 512. Small responses shouldn't include per-token breakdowns.
raul: Agreed. Suggest token_usage.summary -> {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens}. full_token_breakdown only on header or sampled.
sara-pm: We need a concrete minimal response sketch for docs. I drafted this:

```
{
  "id": "resp_123",
  "object": "response",
  "model": "redwood/rtx-1.2",
  "trace_id": "t-9a8b7c",
  "output": "...",
  "token_summary": {"prompt_tokens":"24","completion_tokens":"38","total_tokens":"62"}
}
```

Full metadata object available at /v1/responses/:id?expand=metadata or via header X-include-metadata: full
anya: Good. Add note: trace_id must be stable across retries and have a short prefix to indicate origin (hosted/dedicated/private) — helps downstream routing without carrying full hints.
mike: On naming: prefer token_summary over token_usage since it implies an aggregate. Add a top-level field metadata_version to allow forward compatibility.
raul: We also need a field that signals sampling: metadata.flags: ["trace_sampled"] when full_trace is present.
sara-pm: Will put together a PRD item with success metrics: reduce median response payload by 22% for mobile sample, maintain debuggability for enterprise, <3% support tickets due to missing telemetry.
anya: rollout plan: stage 1 docs + dev preview, stage 2 opt-in header (no alias toggles), stage 3 default minimal (with aliases), stage 4 deprecation of old fields. timeline: Q2 dev preview, Q3 default flip, Q4 deprecation start.
mike: Dev notes: add server-side flag for sampling rate per customer; default 0.01. Also log an audit entry when full metadata returned for compliance.
raul: Implementation notes: runtime will prune fields in serialization layer. keep internal traces untouched. add API gateway param to strip optional fields before signing.
sara-pm: I'll sync with eng-privacy and support. @anya please open the RFC PR and assign reviewers: @mike, @raul, @legal.
anya: On it. PR link coming. tl;dr: minimal envelope + header opt-in + sampling + aliasing for backward compat. :white_check_mark:
